metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable entry point (src/PAYRUN.cbl PROCEDURE DIVISION / MAIN-PARA / STOP RUN) plus its job-execution definition (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl EXEC PGM=PAYRUN). No sibling service units and no resource-provisioning IaC.
metadata.archetype_justification: The program owns and mutates persistent state - reads the indexed EMPMAST master and writes a new PAYOUT generation, with a DB2 backing store per README.md. No queue consumers and no multi-service coordination, so stateful-crud (also the conservative default).
metadata.surface_flag_rationale: Persistent store: DB2 for z/OS (README.md) and VSAM/GDG datasets (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl). At-rest surface: payroll datasets containing EMP-SSN/EMP-ACCT. Deployed workload: production CA-7 schedule PAYRUN-BW. No API surface (batch FTP only). Single mainframe job and single EC2 gateway, so no multi-instance deployment. No Terraform/CloudFormation/CDK/SAM anywhere in the repo.

classification.rationale: This repo has 12 High, 22 Medium, and 0 Low findings. MOD classification is softer than ARA on a single High - in ARA a single High is an agent-deployment gate, whereas in MOD a single High is typically one modernization gap and maps only to Pilot-Ready. This repo is not classified on a single High; it carries twelve, spanning compute, data, security baseline, and delivery automation. Score band 1.34 (Not Ready) agrees with the count-based tier.

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: A plaintext FTP password (payroll PayR0ll2003!) is committed in jcl/PAYRUN.jcl.
top_gaps.impact: Live credential in version control for the host receiving SSN and bank-account data; must be rotated before any migration work begins.

top_gaps.title: Encryption at Rest
top_gaps.gap: No encryption configured for the payroll datasets or the EC2 gateway /incoming/payout.dat, which carry SSN and bank account numbers.
top_gaps.impact: Sensitive PII unprotected at rest and in transit (plain FTP, ascii mode); blocks compliance sign-off on any modernization target.

top_gaps.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
top_gaps.gap: DB2 for z/OS v10 is past end of support (EOS April 2020) per README.md.
top_gaps.impact: No security patches available; forces a database migration as a prerequisite, not an option.

top_gaps.title: Managed Compute
top_gaps.gap: All compute is a z/OS mainframe batch job plus one manually-provisioned EC2 m4.large gateway.
top_gaps.impact: No elasticity for the shrinking batch window; mainframe skills scarcity is a continuity risk.

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: A single COBOL program with all payroll logic in one PROCEDURE DIVISION over shared WORKING-STORAGE and flat files.
top_gaps.impact: No module boundaries to extract against; decomposition requires boundary discovery before any refactor.

decomposition_strategy.recommended_approach: Strengthen as Modular Monolith first (phase 1), then Strangler Fig (phase 2); Conditional/Adaptive replatform-first if continuity risk dominates.

approaches.name: Strengthen as Modular Monolith
approaches.rationale: Extracting named COBOL subprograms (tax calculation, FICA, record formatting, file I/O) and externalizing the literal rate constants addresses the manual January tax-table updates and the state-tax lookup removed in 2011. Safest start given no tests and no boundaries.

approaches.name: Strangler Fig (Parallel Track)
approaches.rationale: Target approach once a golden-file regression suite exists. First extraction is the file gateway/distribution path, then tax calculation behind an anti-corruption layer translating the 120-byte fixed-width record.

approaches.name: Conditional / Adaptive
approaches.rationale: Replatform via AWS Mainframe Modernization to get off scarce-skills hardware without rewriting payroll math - buys time on DB2 EOS and COBOL skills risk.

approaches.name: Big-Bang Rewrite
approaches.rationale: Recommended against: no regression baseline, undocumented manual state-tax rules, retired original authors, and payroll miscalculation is a legally material defect.

patterns.name: Anti-corruption Layer
patterns.purpose: Prevent the 120-byte fixed-width PAY-RECORD layout and 9-digit SSN keys from leaking into new services.

patterns.name: Saga
patterns.purpose: Coordinate pay run -> disbursement -> notification once separated, replacing single-job atomicity.

patterns.name: Event Sourcing
patterns.purpose: Give each pay run an auditable event history, replacing PAYOUT(+1) generation datasets as the de facto audit trail.

patterns.name: Hexagonal Architecture
patterns.purpose: Keep payroll calculation rules testable and independent of DB2/VSAM/file adapters.

effort_factors.signal: Single PROCEDURE DIVISION, shared WORKING-STORAGE, no subprograms (APP-Q2 = 1)
VSAM master plus DB2, file I/O interleaved with logic (DATA-Q2 = 2)
Single nightly FTP file push, no async primitives (APP-Q3 = 2)

decomposition_strategy.calibrated_estimate: Phase 1 (modularize in place, golden-file regression harness, externalize tax tables and credentials) is Low-to-Medium effort and unblocks everything else. Phase 2 (Strangler Fig extraction, or replatform-first if continuity risk forces it) is High effort, dominated by the absent regression baseline and undocumented manual tax rules rather than code volume.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute is unmanaged. The payroll workload runs as a z/OS mainframe batch job (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl: '//STEP010 EXEC PGM=PAYRUN', REGION=0M) scheduled by CA-7, and the only cloud compute is a single manually-provisioned EC2 m4.large file gateway (README.md). No aws_ecs_*, aws_eks_*, aws_lambda_*, Dockerfile, or Kubernetes manifest exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: Zero managed container or serverless adoption; the EC2 gateway is a previous-generation instance family with no definition in code.
findings.recommendation: Replatform the batch onto AWS Mainframe Modernization (managed runtime) or a containerized COBOL runtime on ECS Fargate, and move the file gateway to a managed receive path (S3 + Transfer Family) so the EC2 instance can be retired.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The database is self-managed IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 on the mainframe (README.md), with employee master data also held in a self-managed VSAM indexed dataset (src/PAYRUN.cbl 'ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED'; jcl/PAYRUN.jcl '//EMPMAST DD DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST'). No managed database resource is defined.
findings.gap: 100% self-managed data tier: manual patching, manual backup, no automated failover, and DB2 credentials hardcoded in the job stream.
findings.recommendation: Plan a migration to a managed engine using AWS SCT and DMS. RDS for Db2 preserves the dialect with least change risk; Aurora PostgreSQL is the target if engine change is in scope. Replicate the VSAM master into the same managed store for a single system of record.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated (stateful-crud column applied: the bar is a dedicated orchestration service for business-critical multi-step operations). The pay run is multi-step (calculate -> write PAYOUT -> FTP push) expressed as sequential JCL steps (STEP010, STEP020) triggered by CA-7 schedule PAYRUN-BW. That yields named, ordered steps under a scheduler, but no orchestration service providing retry policy, per-step error handling, state inspection, or partial restart.
findings.gap: No retry, compensation, or restart semantics: if STEP020 (FTP) fails after STEP010 wrote a new PAYOUT generation, recovery is manual. Step state is not observable.
findings.recommendation: Model the pay run as an AWS Step Functions state machine (calculate -> validate -> publish -> notify) with per-state retry and catch, replacing CA-7 sequencing with EventBridge Scheduler.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated (stateful-crud column applied: the bar is managed messaging for cross-service state changes). State crosses a service boundary every run via a plain-FTP file push to a hardcoded IP (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl: 'EXEC PGM=FTP', 'open 10.0.7.40', 'put ... /incoming/payout.dat'). No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Kinesis, MSK, or Amazon MQ resource exists, and no self-managed broker exists either.
findings.gap: Cross-boundary state propagation has no broker, no delivery guarantee, no retry, and no dead-letter path - a failed transfer is silent until someone notices a missing or stale gateway file.
findings.recommendation: Replace the FTP push with an S3 PutObject plus an S3 event notification to EventBridge/SQS, giving durable handoff, retry, and dead-letter semantics.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network controls are defined or evidenced. There is no aws_vpc, aws_subnet, aws_security_group, VPC endpoint, or NetworkPolicy anywhere in the repo, and the only network path in evidence is an unencrypted FTP session to a hardcoded private IP (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl 'open 10.0.7.40') carrying SSN and bank-account data in ascii mode. README.md confirms plaintext FTP of SSN and bank account data.
findings.gap: No segmentation, no least-privilege security groups, no transport encryption, and no network definition under version control for the EC2 gateway terminating this flow.
findings.recommendation: Codify the gateway VPC, private subnets, and least-privilege security groups in IaC; replace FTP with SFTP/FTPS via AWS Transfer Family or an S3 PutObject over a VPC endpoint so the payload never traverses an unencrypted channel.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: There is no managed entry point. The only ingress to the EC2 gateway is a direct FTP connection to its IP address (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl 'open 10.0.7.40'). No API Gateway, AppSync, ALB, or CloudFront resource is defined - the repo contains no IaC at all.
findings.gap: No throttling, authentication, request validation, or health checking in front of the service that receives payroll PII.
findings.recommendation: When the gateway is modernized, front the file-receive path with AWS Transfer Family (managed SFTP with IAM-backed auth) or, for a request/response surface, API Gateway with an authorizer and throttling.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: All capacity is static. The mainframe job requests a fixed region (REGION=0M) and fixed dataset space (SPACE=(CYL,(50,10),RLSE)), and the EC2 gateway is a fixed m4.large (README.md). No aws_autoscaling_*, aws_appautoscaling_*, ASG, or scaling policy exists.
findings.gap: No ability to add capacity when the 5-7 hour batch window tightens, and no scale-down when idle - README.md records that the batch sometimes overruns.
findings.recommendation: After replatforming, parallelize the pay run by employee-range shards on ECS/Fargate or Lambda with concurrency limits, and apply application auto-scaling to the managed database tier.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration exists. The output dataset uses a GDG generation (DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT(+1), DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE)), which retains prior generations as a side effect of job design but is not a backup policy - there is no stated retention, no PITR, no backup plan, and no restore procedure. The employee master EMPMAST has no backup definition at all.
findings.gap: No defined retention, no point-in-time recovery for DB2 or VSAM, no documented or tested restore path for payroll data.
findings.recommendation: Define retention and PITR on the migrated managed database, bring the data stores under AWS Backup with a documented plan, and schedule an annual restore test ahead of a pay run.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: The workload is single-instance end to end: one mainframe batch job and one EC2 m4.large gateway (README.md), with no AZ configuration, no second instance, and no load balancer (has_multi_instance_deployment=false). No multi_az or availability_zones configuration exists because the repo contains no IaC.
findings.gap: Any failure of the gateway host or the mainframe LPAR stops payroll distribution with no automatic recovery; DB2 failover is a manual mainframe operation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the modernized gateway across two or more AZs behind a managed endpoint and enable Multi-AZ on the migrated managed database.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: There is no IaC. Searched the repo root, src/, and jcl/ for *.tf, *.tfvars, template.yaml/json, cdk.json, Chart.yaml, kustomization.yaml, and Ansible playbooks - none found. The repository contains exactly four files: .gitignore, README.md, jcl/PAYRUN.jcl, src/PAYRUN.cbl. The EC2 m4.large gateway in README.md is therefore ClickOps, and the compute, networking, data, and monitoring surfaces this service depends on have no IaC coverage. JCL defines job execution, not infrastructure provisioning.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage against four dependent infrastructure categories; no reproducible environment and no DR rebuild path.
findings.recommendation: Codify the gateway, its network, and the target database in CloudFormation or CDK as the first deliverable of the DevOps workstream, keeping infrastructure changes in the same repository as the application.

evidence.file: *.tf / template.yaml / Chart.yaml (searched repo root, src/, jcl/ - not found)

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD exists. Searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml - none present. Deployment is a manual mainframe recompile into a shared load library (//STEPLIB DD DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.LOADLIB), gated socially rather than technically by the source comment 'DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM'. README.md records no source control until 2021 and validation only in a shared QA region.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, deploy, or rollback artifact, for either application code or infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a pipeline that builds the COBOL in a pinned, reproducible toolchain image, runs a golden-file regression suite, and promotes a versioned load module; add an IaC stage once infrastructure is codified.

evidence.file: .github/workflows/ / buildspec.yml / Jenkinsfile (searched repo root - not found)

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: The system is written in COBOL (Enterprise COBOL 4.2 per README.md) with JCL as job control. src/PAYRUN.cbl is a standard mainframe COBOL program (IDENTIFICATION DIVISION, PROCEDURE DIVISION). There is no AWS SDK and effectively no cloud-native tooling ecosystem for this stack, which the rubric scores as 1. README.md adds that COBOL skills are scarce and the original authors retired.
findings.gap: No AWS SDK availability, no modern dependency or package management, no test framework ecosystem, and a shrinking talent pool for the only language in the system.
findings.recommendation: Treat language transition as a deliberate program: use AWS Transform / AWS Mainframe Modernization code analysis to inventory and convert COBOL to Java or .NET, or replatform onto a managed COBOL runtime as an interim step while conversion proceeds behind a regression harness.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: src/PAYRUN.cbl is a tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. One PROCEDURE DIVISION holds the whole pay run; its three paragraphs (MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-EMP, READ-EMP) communicate only through shared mutable WORKING-STORAGE (WS-GROSS, WS-FICA, WS-NET, WS-EOF). There are no called subprograms and no interfaces, and business rules are literals (WS-FICA-RATE VALUE 0.0620, WS-WAGE-BASE VALUE 132900.00). Calculation, record formatting, and file I/O are interleaved in the same paragraph.
findings.gap: No boundaries to extract against, pervasive shared state, and business rules indistinguishable from data declarations - the hardest starting point for decomposition.
findings.recommendation: Start with in-place modularization: extract tax/FICA calculation, record formatting, and file I/O into separate COBOL subprograms with explicit parameter interfaces, and externalize rate constants into a tax table. See the Decomposition Strategy section.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated (stateful-crud column applied; this archetype expects managed async for cross-service state propagation with sync reads where appropriate). The whole pay run is itself a scheduled background job, which is why this is not a Score 1 - but the single cross-boundary interaction is a blocking in-job FTP push to a fixed host (STEP020), with no broker, no queue, and no event emission on state change. There are no HTTP/gRPC clients and no message publishers in src/PAYRUN.cbl.
findings.gap: Batch-level asynchrony exists by accident of scheduling, not by design; the actual handoff is a tightly-coupled blocking transfer with no decoupling primitive.
findings.recommendation: Emit a payroll-run-completed event (EventBridge) and let consumers pull the output from S3, decoupling distribution from the calculation job.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated (stateful-crud column applied; this archetype expects operations over 30 seconds to run as async jobs with status polling or callbacks). The pay run is a background batch job rather than a blocking foreground call - hence Score 2 rather than 1 - but it has no status surface, no checkpointing, and no restart capability: MAIN-PARA opens files, loops to end-of-file, and stops. README.md reports runs of 5-7 hours that sometimes overrun the shrinking batch window.
findings.gap: Inconsistent long-running-job patterns: no progress or status API and no checkpoint/restart, so an overrun or mid-run failure means re-running from the beginning.
findings.recommendation: Shard the run by employee range with per-shard checkpointing, orchestrate with Step Functions, and expose run status (progress, records processed, failures) so overruns are detected in-flight.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: There is no versioning of any interface contract. The integration contract is a 120-byte fixed-width record (src/PAYRUN.cbl '01 PAY-RECORD PIC X(120)'; jcl/PAYRUN.jcl 'DCB=(RECFM=FB,LRECL=120)') written to a fixed filename (/incoming/payout.dat). No OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL spec, schema file, or version marker exists. README.md lists fixed-width file formats with no schema/versioning as a known issue.
findings.gap: Any field addition or reordering silently breaks every downstream consumer - there is no version negotiation and no schema to validate against.
findings.recommendation: Publish an explicit versioned schema for the payout record (e.g. a versioned JSON/Avro contract with the fixed-width layout documented as v1) and include a version identifier in the filename or payload so consumers can migrate independently.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints are hardcoded. The gateway address is a literal IP in the job stream (open 10.0.7.40), as are the dataset names (ACME.PAYROLL.EMPMAST, ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT, ACME.PAYROLL.LOADLIB) and the remote path (/incoming/payout.dat). README.md confirms hardcoded dataset names and credentials in JCL. No service registry, mesh, or DNS-based discovery is present.
findings.gap: Relocating or replacing the gateway requires editing and redeploying the job stream; there is not even an indirection layer such as environment variables or DNS.
findings.recommendation: Introduce indirection immediately - resolve the destination via DNS or AWS Cloud Map / SSM Parameter Store rather than a literal IP, so the endpoint can change without a code change.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Unstructured and semi-structured output lives on mainframe-local storage and paper, not object storage. Outputs are fixed-width flat files and printed checks via line printer (README.md), written to catalogued datasets (DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.PAYOUT(+1), SYSOUT=*) and then FTP'd onto a single EC2 instance's local filesystem (/incoming/payout.dat). No aws_s3_bucket, Textract call, or document-parsing library appears anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: Payroll artifacts are inaccessible to analytics, search, or lifecycle/retention policy, and durability depends on a single host filesystem plus mainframe generation datasets.
findings.recommendation: Land all payroll outputs in S3 (versioned, encrypted, lifecycle-managed) as the system of record for artifacts, replacing the FTP-to-local-disk handoff; add Textract only if printed documents need re-ingestion.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Access is partially structured but not abstracted. src/PAYRUN.cbl declares both files centrally in FILE-CONTROL/FILE SECTION, giving a single declaration point, but the I/O is interleaved with business logic in the procedure code (READ EMP-FILE inside READ-EMP, WRITE PAY-RECORD inside PROCESS-EMP) and record layouts are positional field definitions rather than an interface. No DB2 access layer is visible in this repo despite README.md stating the batch runs against DB2 - the relational access path is outside the repository.
findings.gap: No data-access abstraction to swap storage engines behind, and at least one access path (DB2) is not discoverable from this repo, which will hide work during migration.
findings.recommendation: Extract file and database I/O into dedicated COBOL subprograms (or a service module post-conversion) exposing record-level operations, and inventory all out-of-repo DB2 access paths before planning the database migration.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: The engine is past end of support and the version is not pinned anywhere machine-readable. README.md states 'IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 (out of support)' and lists DB2 v10 end of support (EOS April 2020) as a known issue. The version appears only in prose - there is no IaC parameter, image tag, or Helm value pinning it, because the repo contains no IaC.
findings.gap: An unsupported database engine receives no security patches, and with no version pinning in code there is no guardrail against drift or surprise during migration.
findings.recommendation: Treat the DB2 v10 EOS as the forcing function for the Move to Managed Databases pathway: pin the target engine version explicitly in IaC and migrate to a supported managed engine (RDS for Db2 for minimum change, Aurora PostgreSQL if engine change is in scope) via SCT/DMS.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest is configured on any data surface, and the data is highly sensitive: the employee record carries SSN and bank account number (EMP-SSN PIC 9(09), EMP-ACCT PIC X(17)). Payroll datasets are written with no encryption attributes, and the output is deposited on the EC2 gateway local filesystem as /incoming/payout.dat. No aws_kms_key, kms_key_id, or dataset-encryption directive exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: SSN and bank-account data sits unencrypted at rest on both the mainframe datasets and the gateway host, with no key management, rotation policy, or access audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt both ends immediately: enable z/OS pervasive encryption on the payroll datasets, and replace the gateway local-disk landing zone with an S3 bucket using a customer-managed KMS key with a documented rotation policy.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: The system exposes no HTTP/gRPC API (has_api_surface=false), so the authenticated surface in scope is the FTP integration endpoint on the gateway. That endpoint uses static username/password credentials supplied inline (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl 'payroll PayR0ll2003!') - static-credential authentication, which the rubric scores as 2 - with no token-based auth, no per-request authorization, and no authorizer in front of it.
findings.gap: A single long-lived shared credential authenticates all payroll data transfer; there is no per-request attribution, expiry, or revocation path.
findings.recommendation: Replace static FTP credentials with IAM-backed access - AWS Transfer Family with IAM/service-managed identities, or direct S3 PutObject under an IAM role - so every transfer is attributable and credentials are short-lived.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Authentication is entirely local to each system with no external identity provider. The job stream authenticates to the gateway with its own embedded username/password and to DB2 with separate hardcoded credentials (jcl/PAYRUN.jcl header: 'DATASET NAMES AND DB2 CREDS HARDCODED'). No aws_cognito_*, OIDC, SAML, or federation configuration exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: No centralized identity, no SSO, and no single place to revoke access - each integration point manages its own standalone credential.
findings.recommendation: Federate machine access to IAM roles (IAM Roles Anywhere or AWS Transfer Family service-managed identities) and bring human operator access under the organization's central IdP via IAM Identity Center.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: A plaintext production credential is committed to version control: jcl/PAYRUN.jcl line 18 contains 'payroll PayR0ll2003!' inside the FTP SYSIN stream, authenticating to the host that receives SSN and bank-account data. The same file's header states 'DATASET NAMES AND DB2 CREDS HARDCODED - SEE OPS RUNBOOK', and README.md lists hardcoded credentials in JCL as a known issue. No aws_secretsmanager_* resource, Vault client, or parameter-store reference exists. Plaintext credential presence is Score 1 by rule.
findings.gap: A live, unrotated credential is in git history and readable by anyone with repository access; there is no secrets store, no rotation, and no audit trail of credential use.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the FTP and DB2 credentials now, treating them as compromised. Move them into AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation and have the job retrieve them at runtime; purge the credential from git history. This is the highest-priority, lowest-effort remediation in this report.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching or vulnerability-scanning strategy is evidenced. No aws_ssm_patch_baseline, SSM agent configuration, hardened AMI reference, EC2 Image Builder pipeline, Inspector configuration, or Dependabot/Renovate config exists. The evidence points the other way: DB2 is past end of support (README.md), the gateway is a previous-generation m4.large with no documented AMI or patch cadence, and src/PAYRUN.cbl carries 'WARNING: DO NOT RECOMPILE WITHOUT CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM', indicating patching is actively discouraged.
findings.gap: No managed patching, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened base image, and an organizational constraint that treats rebuilding as risky.
findings.recommendation: Bring the gateway under SSM Patch Manager with a hardened base AMI and enable Amazon Inspector; establish a reproducible COBOL build (pinned compiler image in CI) so recompilation stops being a risk event and patching becomes routine.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: There is no pipeline, therefore no security validation step. Searched for .github/workflows/, buildspec.yml, Jenkinsfile, .snyk, .github/dependabot.yml, and renovate.json - none found. No SAST, dependency scanning, or container/image scanning is configured. A secret-scanning gate would have caught the plaintext credential in jcl/PAYRUN.jcl (SEC-Q5) before it was committed.
findings.gap: No automated security gate of any kind; the plaintext credential already in the repository is direct evidence of the consequence.
findings.recommendation: Add secret scanning as the first pipeline gate (blocking), then SAST appropriate to the stack and image scanning for the containerized gateway, with builds failing on critical findings.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation exists. The only runtime output is unstructured print output (//SYSOUT DD SYSOUT=*). No OpenTelemetry SDK, X-Ray instrumentation, or correlation/trace identifier appears in src/PAYRUN.cbl or jcl/PAYRUN.jcl, and the mainframe-to-gateway FTP hop propagates no context.
findings.gap: A pay run cannot be traced across the mainframe-to-gateway boundary; failure diagnosis depends on reading SYSOUT and inspecting files by hand.
findings.recommendation: Emit a correlation ID per pay run (run date plus sequence) into structured logs on both the batch and gateway sides, forwarded to CloudWatch Logs; adopt OpenTelemetry/X-Ray as components are replatformed.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: Evaluated because has_persistent_data_store=true (the OR branch of the gate; there is no API surface). No monitoring artifacts of any kind exist in the repo - no CloudWatch alarm definitions, latency or error-rate thresholds, SLO file, or dashboard definition. The only service-level expectation is prose: a biweekly batch window that the run sometimes overruns at 5-7 hours (README.md). Per rubric guidance, Score 1 applies because no monitoring artifacts exist at all.
findings.gap: The one genuinely critical service level - pay run completes before the batch window closes - is neither defined numerically nor measured.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit SLO for pay-run completion time (and payout-file delivery success) with an error budget, and instrument it as a CloudWatch alarm on job duration so overruns alert in-flight.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are published. src/PAYRUN.cbl computes per-employee gross, FICA, and net pay but emits no counters or totals - not even a control total of records processed or sum of net pay; the loop writes records until end-of-file. The only operational output is SYSOUT=*. No put_metric_data equivalent, dashboard, or KPI alarm exists.
findings.gap: No measurement of payroll business outcomes (employees paid, total disbursed, calculation exceptions), so a partial or wrong run is not detectable from telemetry.
findings.recommendation: Publish per-run control totals (records processed, total gross/net, exception count) as custom CloudWatch metrics and alarm on deviation from the prior run - the standard safeguard for batch payroll correctness.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The job's only notification mechanism is the MVS console/TSO notify on the JOB card (NOTIFY=&SYSUID), which messages the submitting user ID rather than an on-call rotation. No CloudWatch alarm, anomaly detector, composite alarm, or PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration exists. README.md notes overruns are discovered operationally, not by alert.
findings.gap: No automated detection of job failure, overrun, FTP transfer failure, or output-volume anomaly; detection depends on a person noticing.
findings.recommendation: Alarm on job exit status, run duration, and payout-file arrival/size at the gateway, routed to an on-call destination via SNS; add CloudWatch anomaly detection on run duration and record counts once metrics exist (OPS-Q3).

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: Evaluated because has_deployed_workload=true - the job runs in production on CA-7 schedule PAYRUN-BW. Deployment is direct-to-production with no staged rollout: a recompiled load module is placed into the single shared library the job loads from (//STEPLIB DD DSN=ACME.PAYROLL.LOADLIB,DISP=SHR), so the next scheduled run picks up the change wholesale. There is no traffic shifting, canary, parallel run, or versioned rollback artifact; README.md records validation only in a shared QA region.
findings.gap: No mechanism to limit the blast radius of a bad payroll change - the first production exercise of new logic is a real pay run affecting every employee.
findings.recommendation: Adopt parallel-run verification as the batch equivalent of canary: execute the new load module against production input in a shadow run and diff the output against the current module before promotion; keep versioned load modules so rollback is a pointer change.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: There are no automated tests at all. README.md states 'No automated tests; changes validated in a shared QA region only'. The repository contains four files (.gitignore, README.md, jcl/PAYRUN.jcl, src/PAYRUN.cbl) - no test directory, test JCL, sample EMPMAST fixtures, or expected-output datasets. There is also no CI pipeline for tests to run in (INF-Q11).
findings.gap: No regression baseline for a payroll calculation. This is the dominant risk multiplier for every modernization pathway: COBOL conversion, database migration, and replatforming all require proof of output equivalence, and none exists.
findings.recommendation: Build a golden-file regression harness first: a representative synthetic EMPMAST fixture set (including boundary cases such as the FICA wage-base cap at 132900.00) with checked-in expected PAYOUT output, executed in CI on every change. Treat this as the prerequisite deliverable before any other modernization work.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: Evaluated because has_deployed_workload=true. A runbook exists as documentation but is neither automated nor version-controlled here: jcl/PAYRUN.jcl line 4 directs operators to 'SEE OPS RUNBOOK', and src/PAYRUN.cbl line 5 escalates by instruction. No SSM Automation document, Lambda remediation, Step Functions incident workflow, or machine-readable runbook file is present in the repo.
findings.gap: Response is manual and depends on an out-of-repo document plus tribal knowledge from a team whose COBOL expertise README.md describes as scarce - the key-person risk is structural.
findings.recommendation: Bring the runbook into the repository as structured versioned content, then automate the recurring responses (job-overrun escalation, FTP retry, re-run from checkpoint) as SSM Automation documents so recovery does not depend on individual recall.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability assets exist to own, and no ownership is declared. There is no CODEOWNERS file, dashboard or alarm definition, or SLO file with team attribution (searched repo root and .github/). Ownership signals in the repo are informal and point to absent people: the author of src/PAYRUN.cbl is annotated 'R. ANDERSON (RETIRED 2014)' and escalation is 'CONTACTING MAINFRAME TEAM'.
findings.gap: No named owner for monitoring, no per-service dashboard, and the documented ownership trail leads to retired staff.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file naming the accountable team, and create an owned per-service dashboard (run duration, record counts, transfer success) with alarms tagged to that team as observability assets are built out.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL constructs found. Searched src/ and jcl/ for *.sql, CREATE PROCEDURE/TRIGGER/FUNCTION, and EXEC SQL - none found. All payroll business logic is in the COBOL application layer (src/PAYRUN.cbl COMPUTE statements).

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false - the repo provisions no AWS resources and contains no account/foundation-level IaC. CloudTrail is an account-level service; evaluation belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false - the repo provisions no AWS resources, so there is nothing to tag. Tagging governance belongs in the repo that owns the AWS infrastructure.
